back: An expense incurred in the period but not yet paid at the year end; a current liability (other payables).
Payment made in the period for a benefit that belongs to a later period; a current asset (other receivables).
Income earned in the period but not yet received; a current asset.
Cash received for a future period; a current liability.
Cash paid + opening prepayment + closing accrual - opening accrual - closing prepayment.
Cash received + opening income received in advance + closing accrued income - opening accrued income - closing income received in advance.

front: Which concept supports accruals and prepayments?
back: Matching (accruals): costs and revenue belong to the period in which they arise, not when cash moves.

front: Effect on profit of an omitted accrued expense
back: Expenses understated, profit overstated and liabilities understated.

front: Where does a closing prepayment sit in an expense account?
back: Balance c/d on the credit side; brought down on the debit side as an asset.
